Recipe for Potato Dumplings (Varenyky) Ingredients: For the dough: Wheat flour 每 500 g Water 每 200 ml Egg 每 1 Salt 每 1 tsp For the filling: Potatoes 每 1 kg Onions 每 2 Lard or butter 每 50 g Salt 每 to taste Ground black pepper 每 to taste Preparation steps: Making the dough: Sifting the flour: Sift the flour into a large bowl. Making the dough: Add salt and the egg to the flour. Gradually pour in the water, constantly stirring. Knead the dough until it becomes smooth and elastic. Resting the dough: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap or cover it with a towel and let it rest for 30 minutes. Preparing the filling: Boiling the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut them into large pieces, and boil until tender in salted water. Preparing the onions: While the potatoes are boiling, finely chop the onions. Saut谷 the onions in lard or butter until golden brown. Making the potato puree: Drain the potatoes and mash them. Add the saut谷ed onions, salt, and pepper to taste, and mix well. Forming the dumplings: Rolling out the dough: Roll out the dough into a thin sheet about 2-3 mm thick. Use a glass or cutter to cut out circles approximately 7-8 cm in diameter. Forming the dumplings: Place a spoonful of potato filling on each circle of dough. Fold the dough in half and pinch the edges tightly to seal the dumplings. Cooking the dumplings: Boiling water: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add salt. Cooking the dumplings: Gently drop the dumplings into the boiling water, stirring carefully to prevent sticking. Cook until done (approximately 5-7 minutes after they float to the surface). Serving: Removing the dumplings: Remove the dumplings with a slotted spoon and place them on a plate. Serving: Serve the dumplings hot, optionally drizzling with melted butter, sour cream, or saut谷ed onions. Enjoy your meal!

10/10 I first played Hades when it was in Early Access, and I really liked what I saw back then, but, for external reasons, I ended up leaving the game behind and never really played it again, even though I'd seen the game getting massively positive reviews everywhere (well, of course, the game really IS everything people say it is). This year, I decided to return to Hades with getting 100% completion in mind, since I really wanted to play Hades II, and I wouldn't play it without completing everything in Hades first, so my journey began; The thing is, there is nothing special about my ※journey§ playing Hades, nothing too different from the majority of players' experiences, but the ※conventional§ experience was already enough to make it a blast. I've played a lot of roguelikes in my life (and still do, by the way; it's by far my favorite genre out there), and Hades is easily tied for first place with The Binding of Isaac. I'm not really trying to compare them, but I genuinely can't say one is better than the other, since both are 10/10 in their own ways. The game is just too good. The story itself is phenomenal, and the way it blends with the roguelike genre is also just chef's kiss. There isn't a single character that I didn't end up liking lol. The gameplay itself is also on another level. In my first ten hours I thought the weapons and boons weren't that many but after 70 hours, I can confidently say: there really are that many. It's not that there are a lot of weapons or a massive amount of boons (power-ups) to choose from, but they blend so well with each other and make the gameplay feel so different from before that it's completely worth it. Also, about the story, there's something really cool: the game could technically end earlier if you don't want to spend that much time on it (though I honestly don't know why you wouldn't). The game basically has ※two endings§; the first one starts the credits scene and you could say that's the end of the story if you want, but after that there is the ※post-credits§ section where you can keep playing and the story basically keeps moving forward, more than doubling your playtime. The thing is, if you want to stop there or take a break from the game, you won't really be missing much, at least not nearly as much as if you stopped before the climax, I mean. As someone who deeply loves the roguelike genre, I feel SO happy that Hades exists. As I've said before, to me, Hades is just on another level compared to most other games in the genre. The story is fantastic. The gameplay is some of the most addictive and enjoyable out there. The voice acting and performances of all the characters are more than just on point: it's honestly absurd how good they are. And I WON'T even start talking about the OST, or else I'll never stop (It's also chef's kiss, who would've thought?) Truly a masterpiece. - a fellow Dusa fan

My first playthrough of Elden Ring was on the OG Xbox One which meant barely getting 30fps and 3 - 5 minute loading screens after failing bosses. Not to mention heavy rolling up to Godfrey, First Elden Lord (Golden Shade) until being saved by my friends informing me that I didn't have to do that. I say this because somehow the game was still 10/10 without even playing the damn thing correct and making it EVEN MORE difficult than I needed it to. I then beat Elden Ring (and a few NG+ runs), and I can confidently say it was one of the most rewarding experiences I've had completing a game. I shed a few tears because I didn't think I could do it, and it taught me an odd amount of patience. It is not perfect, and it certainly is not for everyone, but it is incredible, and I haven't played anything quite like it. My PC playthrough has been fun, the DLC is truly amazing (although I do have some complaints), and 60fps is like taking off ankle weights, but sadly stutter is a very real issue for this game, and that is something that should've been fixed long before now. Maybe it's just my pc though.
